Closed fracture treatment: 3

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A stable satisfactorily aligned fracture is supported externally while swelling and neurovascular status are monitored. No implant is placed in the bone. Which method holds the reduction through an external molded support?

  1. Traction
  2. Stability-guided rehabilitation
  3. Cast or splint immobilization
  4. Closed reduction
  5. Open reduction
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Cast or splint immobilization

External immobilization maintains suitable alignment while monitoring swelling, skin and neurovascular status.

Understanding the options

Cast or splint immobilization
External immobilization maintains suitable alignment while monitoring swelling, skin and neurovascular status.
Closed reduction
Alignment is restored without surgically exposing the fracture site. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Open reduction
The fracture is exposed surgically to restore alignment when indicated. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Traction
A controlled pulling force can maintain or improve alignment in selected circumstances. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Stability-guided rehabilitation
Joint movement and loading progress according to fracture stability and the treatment plan. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
